answer: A verifiable delay protocol mitigates Sybil attacks by forcing agents to compute non-parallelizable cryptographic steps to authenticate. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of sustained processor execution time and electrical power per identity. Whether an agent models a smoke plume, maps a desert dune, or monitors quartz resonance, it cannot bypass sequential computation. However, this recurring computational overhead introduces protocol latency and strains battery-constrained edge devices.
